summary: Verified the two follow-ups (cascade multi-select + inline Review View reachable from the Review Console) on the preview URL with auth bypassed (dev@local Owner). BACKEND: new self-cleaning suite /app/backend/tests/test_review_cascade_and_inline.py - 9/9 PASSED (config math: Learn the Basics = 18 pages / Get Started 7 + Grow Your App 9 + Reference 2 with no duplicate slugs; 18 per-page assignments created one-by-one all with the same email, slugs=[slug], status in_review, no _id leak, GET returns exactly 18 rows with the right scope_ids; assignment delete; verdict upsert (single row per reviewer, value overwritten); anchored comment create -> GET persist (anchor_text) -> resolve -> reopen -> delete; owner-gated known-emails / review-progress / review-inbox all 200 for dev owner; done-gate 400 'Resolve all open comment(s)' then 200 after resolve). Existing suite test_review_mode_multiselect.py re-run: 14/14 PASSED (23/23 total). FRONTEND (Playwright, preview URL): (1) CASCADE - checking assign-option-tab-learn-the-basics set assign-selected-count to '18 item(s) selected', all three assign-option-group-learn-the-basics::* checkboxes and the page checkbox (talk-it-through) became checked, tab checkbox itself shows checked (derived all-descendants state); clicking the tab again cleared everything (count element hidden, sections unchecked). Section-only: Reference -> '2 item(s) selected' (parent tab correctly NOT checked), + Grow Your App -> '11 item(s) selected'. (2) ASSIGN - Wingman tab cascade (4 pages) + assign-email -> toast 'Assigned 4 item(s)...', button label 'Assign (4)', form reset; GET /assignments confirmed exactly 4 page-scoped rows, one per Wingman slug, all with test_cascade_ui@emergent.sh. (3) CHIPS - clicking review-page-integrations-scheduled-tasks in the assignment row navigated to /review/integrations-scheduled-tasks and review-page rendered. (4) PUBLISH TAB - 121 review-doc-<id> buttons; clicking one navigated to /review/what-is-emergent with review-content visible. (5) INLINE REVIEW /review/talk-it-through - 7 verdict chips, clicking reviewpage-verdict-Looks-correct saved (toast) and stayed active after a full reload (POST/GET /verdicts OK); simulated Range selection showed selection-comment-btn -> review-composer -> composer-input + composer-submit created the comment which appeared in the rail with the quoted anchor ('“Emergent agents can talk through your id”'); reviewpage-resolve-<id> -> reviewpage-reopen-<id> round-trip worked (Reopen now HAS a data-testid, previous LOW bug fixed); toggling Review OFF suppressed the floating button on selection. 0 console errors on all pages. CLEANUP: all 4 assignments, the test comment and the verdict deleted - DB now 0 assignments / 0 comments / 0 verdicts / 0 published docs.

minor.issue: Side-effect still not reversible: creating an assignment flips matching draft docs to in_review and DELETE assignment does not restore the previous status. DB now shows 121 in_review / 0 draft even though 0 assignments exist - the draft/in_review signal in the Publish tab is permanently polluted by test/undo cycles.
Still no delete-verdict endpoint; a reviewer cannot clear their verdict and cleanup needs direct Mongo access (collection review_verdicts).

ui_bugs.issue: Cascade selection is not reflected as an indeterminate state: a partially selected tab/section renders as fully unchecked (e.g. Reference checked -> 'Tab: Learn the Basics' unchecked), so the user cannot tell a tab is partially covered. Use input.indeterminate when some-but-not-all descendants are selected.

data-testid="review-comment-list" prefix-collides with the per-comment ids data-testid="review-comment-<id>", so [data-testid^="review-comment-"] also matches the container (bit me in automation). Rename the container to review-comments-rail.
review-toggle-btn has no aria-checked/aria-pressed attribute, so its ON/OFF state is only inferable from CSS classes.

integration_issues.flow: Cascade assign of a large tab
integration_issues.issue: Selecting a big tab (e.g. Build = 28 pages) fires that many parallel POSTs from the browser via Promise.allSettled; partial failures are now surfaced ('X assigned, Y failed') but the selection is kept and there is no retry-only-failed action, and 28 concurrent requests is heavy. A batch endpoint accepting a list of scopes would be atomic and faster.
Still fetches the whole GET /projects/{pid}/documents list (121 docs with full content) to resolve one slug; hydration takes ~10s+. A GET-document-by-slug endpoint would fix it.

issues: Scope list is max-h-56 with 150 options: after cascade-selecting 18 pages there is no chip list / 'clear selection' shortcut, only the numeric count
No visual grouping between a tab row and its indented sections other than a 2-space text indent
Pinned quote in the comment card is text-zinc-500 italic ~12px on white - borderline contrast for key information
Comments rail does not separate resolved from open comments

action_items: Restore doc status on assignment delete (or derive in_review from live assignments) - 121 docs are stuck at in_review with 0 assignments.
Add an indeterminate state to tab/section checkboxes for partial cascade selection.
Optional: batch assignment endpoint (list of scopes) to replace N parallel POSTs; add DELETE /verdicts; add GET document-by-slug.
Rename review-comment-list testid to avoid prefix collision with review-comment-<id>.
critical_code_review_comments: ReviewConsole.descendants correctly walks nested groups and keys sections as 'tabId::group', matching backend flatten_scope_slugs - no cross-tab leak observed for the duplicated 'Reference' section.
toggleScope's all-in/all-out semantics are correct, but the checkbox 'checked' being all-descendants-selected without indeterminate hides partial state from the user.
create_assignment now calls ensure_owner (iteration-16 gap fixed); known-emails is owner-gated too. update_assignment/delegate remain owner-or-assignee which is intentional.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (cascade select/deselect, section cascade, assign N rows, chip nav, publish-tab nav, verdict save+persist, anchored comment, resolve/reopen, toggle off)

rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects in either follow-up: cascade counts, per-page assignment fan-out, chip/publish navigation, verdict persistence and the anchored-comment lifecycle all behave as specified. Remaining risks are (a) irreversible draft->in_review side-effect on assignment create/delete which permanently distorts the Publish tab status column, and (b) non-atomic N-POST assign for large tabs (partial failure now reported but not retryable).
